title: 1 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 23.

questions.question: Who came to David at Keilah with an ephod in his hand?
options: Abiathar the son of Ahimelech
Jonathan the son of Saul
Saul the king of Israel
A messenger from the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Abiathar the son of Ahimelech
questions.explanation: Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David and came down with an ephod in his hand, as stated in 1 Samuel 23:6.

questions.question: What did David inquire of the LORD concerning the Philistines fighting against Keilah?
options: Shall I flee from Keilah?
Shall I go and smite these Philistines?
Shall I surrender to the Philistines?
Shall I make peace with Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall I go and smite these Philistines?
questions.explanation: David asked the LORD, 'Shall I go and smite these Philistines?' as recorded in 1 Samuel 23:2.

questions.question: What was the reason David's men gave for being afraid to go to Keilah?
options: Because the inhabitants of Keilah were hostile
Because they were afraid in Judah and more so against the armies of the Philistines
Because Saul was pursuing them
Because the wilderness was too dangerous
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were afraid in Judah and more so against the armies of the Philistines
questions.explanation: David's men expressed fear by saying, 'Behold, we be afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?,' as found in 1 Samuel 23:3.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to David the second time he enquired about going to Keilah?
options: Do not go to Keilah
Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand
Hide in the wilderness
Negotiate peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand
questions.explanation: The LORD answered David, instructing him to go down to Keilah because He would deliver the Philistines into David's hand, as stated in 1 Samuel 23:4.

questions.question: What did David and his men do when they came to Keilah?
options: They fled to the wilderness
They fought the Philistines, brought away their cattle, and smote them with great slaughter
They surrendered to Saul’s army
They made peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: They fought the Philistines, brought away their cattle, and smote them with great slaughter
questions.explanation: David and his men fought the Philistines, took their cattle, and smote them with great slaughter, thereby saving the inhabitants of Keilah, as described in 1 Samuel 23:5.

questions.question: What did Saul say when he heard that David had come to Keilah?
options: David will escape easily
God hath delivered him into mine hand; for he is shut in by entering into a town that hath gates and bars
David will make peace with me
I will seek the LORD’s guidance first
questions.correctAnswer: God hath delivered him into mine hand; for he is shut in by entering into a town that hath gates and bars
questions.explanation: Saul believed God had delivered David into his hand because David was confined in a town with gates and bars, as stated in 1 Samuel 23:7.

questions.question: What action did Saul take after hearing David was in Keilah?
options: He ignored the news
He called all the people together to war to besiege David and his men
He sent a messenger to negotiate
He asked David to surrender peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: He called all the people together to war to besiege David and his men
questions.explanation: Saul gathered the people to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men, as described in 1 Samuel 23:8.

questions.question: What did David ask Abiathar to bring to him?
options: A sword
The ephod
A shield
A horse
questions.correctAnswer: The ephod
questions.explanation: David asked Abiathar the priest to bring him the ephod, as recorded in 1 Samuel 23:9.

questions.question: What did David say he had certainly heard about Saul’s intentions?
options: That Saul sought to make peace with him
That Saul sought to come to Keilah to destroy the city for David's sake
That Saul was leaving the land
That Saul was going to fight the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: That Saul sought to come to Keilah to destroy the city for David's sake
questions.explanation: David stated he had heard that Saul sought to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of him, as found in 1 Samuel 23:10.

questions.question: True or False: David and his men were afraid to fight the Philistines at Keilah.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David's men said they were afraid in Judah and even more so if they went to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines, as in 1 Samuel 23:3.

questions.question: True or False: Saul immediately pursued David after he escaped from Keilah.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: After David escaped from Keilah, Saul forbare to go forth, meaning he did not immediately pursue David, as stated in 1 Samuel 23:13.

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan strengthened David's hand in God by visiting him in the wood.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan came to David in the wood and strengthened his hand in God, as recorded in 1 Samuel 23:16.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Keilah would deliver David into Saul's hand according to the LORD's answer.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD told David that the men of Keilah would deliver him into Saul's hand, as found in 1 Samuel 23:12.

questions.question: Which event happened first in 1 Samuel 23?
options: David fought the Philistines at Keilah
Saul called the people to besiege Keilah
Abiathar fled to David with the ephod
David enquired of the LORD if he should go and smite the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: David enquired of the LORD if he should go and smite the Philistines
questions.explanation: The first event was David enquiring of the LORD whether he should go and smite the Philistines, as in 1 Samuel 23:2, before the other events occurred.

questions.question: What did David and his men do after learning that the men of Keilah would deliver them to Saul?
options: They stayed to defend the city
They arose and departed out of Keilah
They sought peace with Saul
They hid in the threshingfloors
questions.correctAnswer: They arose and departed out of Keilah
questions.explanation: Upon learning that the men of Keilah would deliver them to Saul, David and his men arose and departed out of Keilah, as noted in 1 Samuel 23:13.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did David inquire of the LORD before going to smite the Philistines at Keilah?
options: If he should flee from Saul
If he should gather more men
If he should go and smite the Philistines
If he should fortify the city
questions.correctAnswer: If he should go and smite the Philistines
questions.explanation: David asked the LORD whether he should go and smite the Philistines who were fighting against Keilah, and the LORD instructed him to go and save Keilah (1 Samuel 23:2).

questions.question: Why were David’s men afraid to go to Keilah to fight the Philistines?
options: Because they were outnumbered
Because they feared Saul’s army
Because they were afraid in Judah and even more so against the Philistines’ armies
Because they lacked weapons
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were afraid in Judah and even more so against the Philistines’ armies
questions.explanation: David's men expressed fear in Judah and questioned how they could face the Philistine armies at Keilah (1 Samuel 23:3).

questions.question: How did the LORD respond when David asked if he should go down to Keilah to fight?
options: The LORD said to wait for further instruction
The LORD said He would deliver the Philistines into David’s hand
The LORD said not to go because of danger
The LORD was silent
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD said He would deliver the Philistines into David’s hand
questions.explanation: The LORD encouraged David to arise and go down to Keilah, promising to deliver the Philistines into his hand (1 Samuel 23:4).

questions.question: What was the outcome of David’s battle against the Philistines at Keilah?
options: David was defeated and fled
David made peace with the Philistines
David and his men smote the Philistines and saved Keilah
David was captured
questions.correctAnswer: David and his men smote the Philistines and saved Keilah
questions.explanation: David and his men fought the Philistines, brought away their cattle, smote them with great slaughter, and saved the inhabitants of Keilah (1 Samuel 23:5).

questions.question: What did David do when he learned Saul was coming to besiege Keilah?
options: He prepared the city’s defenses
He enquired of the LORD using the ephod
He surrendered to Saul
He fled without counsel
questions.correctAnswer: He enquired of the LORD using the ephod
questions.explanation: David, aware of Saul’s secret plans, asked Abiathar the priest to bring the ephod so he could inquire of the LORD (1 Samuel 23:9).

questions.question: What did the LORD reveal to David about Saul’s intentions toward Keilah?
options: Saul would not come
Saul would come down to destroy Keilah for David’s sake
Saul would negotiate peace
Saul was unaware of David’s location
questions.correctAnswer: Saul would come down to destroy Keilah for David’s sake
questions.explanation: The LORD told David that Saul sought to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of him (1 Samuel 23:10-11).

questions.question: According to the LORD's revelation, what would the men of Keilah do to David and his men?
options: Protect them from Saul
Deliver them into Saul’s hand
Hide them in the city
Help them escape
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver them into Saul’s hand
questions.explanation: The LORD told David that the men of Keilah would deliver him and his men into the hand of Saul (1 Samuel 23:12).

questions.question: What action did David take after learning the men of Keilah would betray him?
options: He fortified the city
He negotiated with Saul
He and his six hundred men departed out of Keilah
He surrendered to Saul
questions.correctAnswer: He and his six hundred men departed out of Keilah
questions.explanation: David and his men, numbering about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah to avoid capture (1 Samuel 23:13).

questions.question: Where did David stay after fleeing from Keilah, and how did God protect him there?
options: In the city of Jerusalem; God did not protect him
In the wilderness in strong holds; God did not deliver him into Saul’s hand
In the Philistine territory; God gave him victory
In the land of Moab; God hid him
questions.correctAnswer: In the wilderness in strong holds; God did not deliver him into Saul’s hand
questions.explanation: David stayed in the wilderness in strong holds, and although Saul sought him daily, God did not deliver David into his hand (1 Samuel 23:14).

questions.question: What encouragement did Jonathan give to David in the wilderness?
options: To hide and never return
To fear Saul’s hand
To fear not, for Saul will not find him and David shall be king
To attack Saul’s army immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To fear not, for Saul will not find him and David shall be king
questions.explanation: Jonathan encouraged David not to fear because Saul would not find him, and he affirmed that David would be king with Jonathan next to him (1 Samuel 23:17).

questions.question: What covenant did David and Jonathan make before the LORD?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David and Jonathan made a covenant before the LORD, strengthening their bond and mutual commitment (1 Samuel 23:18).

questions.question: Did the Ziphites intend to help Saul capture David?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Ziphites informed Saul about David’s hiding places and offered to deliver him into Saul’s hand (1 Samuel 23:19-20).

questions.question: Saul immediately pursued David in the wilderness of Maon without interruption.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Saul pursued David but had to stop and return to fight the Philistines who invaded the land, interrupting his pursuit (1 Samuel 23:25-28).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 23:13–14 illustrate the importance of trusting God's guidance when facing betrayal?
options: David ignored God's warnings and stayed in Keilah
David trusted God's word and escaped betrayal by leaving Keilah and abiding in strong holds
David tried to confront Saul without counsel
David surrendered to Saul because he lost faith
questions.correctAnswer: David trusted God's word and escaped betrayal by leaving Keilah and abiding in strong holds
questions.explanation: After God revealed that Keilah’s men would betray him, David trusted and obeyed by departing and finding refuge, showing faith in God's protection (1 Samuel 23:12-14).

questions.question: What does the interaction between Jonathan and David in verses 16–18 teach about Christian friendship and encouragement?
options: Friends should avoid helping in difficult times
True friendship involves strengthening one another in God and making commitments before the LORD
Friends should compete for leadership
Encouragement is unnecessary in trials
questions.correctAnswer: True friendship involves strengthening one another in God and making commitments before the LORD
questions.explanation: Jonathan strengthened David’s hand in God and they made a covenant before the LORD, exemplifying supportive Christian friendship (1 Samuel 23:16-18).

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 23.

questions.question: What did Saul say to the Ziphites when they offered to help him capture David?
options: Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me
You are cursed for betraying David
I will reward you with riches
You shall be my enemies forever
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me
questions.explanation: Saul expressed gratitude to the Ziphites for their support by saying, 'Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me' as stated in 1 Samuel 23:21.

questions.question: What strategy did Saul instruct his men to use in order to capture David?
options: To prepare and know all David's lurking places and inform him with certainty
To attack David's followers directly in the wilderness
To blockade all roads leading to Engedi
To ambush David at Keilah again
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare and know all David's lurking places and inform him with certainty
questions.explanation: Saul told his men to prepare and find out all the places where David was hiding and to report back with certainty so he could search for him throughout Judah (1 Samuel 23:22-23).

questions.question: Where were David and his men found when Saul and the Ziphites went to seek him?
options: In the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon
At Keilah, defending the city
In strong holds at Engedi
In the hill of Hachilah
questions.correctAnswer: In the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon
questions.explanation: The text states that David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, south of Jeshimon, when Saul and the Ziphites went to seek him (1 Samuel 23:24).

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 23, what caused Saul to stop pursuing David?
options: A messenger informed Saul that the Philistines had invaded the land
David escaped into a stronghold
Jonathan pleaded with Saul to stop
Saul was injured and had to retreat
questions.correctAnswer: A messenger informed Saul that the Philistines had invaded the land
questions.explanation: Saul ceased chasing David because a messenger brought news that the Philistines had invaded, prompting Saul to return and fight them (1 Samuel 23:27-28).

questions.question: What covenant is described in 1 Samuel 23 between David and Jonathan?
options: A covenant before the LORD confirming Jonathan’s support and friendship
A political alliance against Saul
An agreement to divide the kingdom after Saul’s death
A secret pact to overthrow Saul
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant before the LORD confirming Jonathan’s support and friendship
questions.explanation: David and Jonathan made a covenant before the LORD, symbolizing Jonathan’s support and friendship despite Saul’s hostility (1 Samuel 23:18). This covenant foreshadows the Messianic kingship of David.

questions.question: What did Jonathan say to David to strengthen him in God?
options: Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel
We shall defeat Saul together and rule as kings
You will never be king, but I will protect you
God has forsaken Saul, and you must flee
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel
questions.explanation: Jonathan encouraged David to fear not because Saul’s hand would not find him, affirming David’s future as king (1 Samuel 23:17). This reflects the biblical theme of divine protection and prophetic kingship.

questions.question: Which place is named Selahammahlekoth and why?
options: The place where Saul stopped pursuing David because of the Philistine invasion
The stronghold where David hid from Saul
The city David saved from the Philistines
The mountain where Jonathan met David
questions.correctAnswer: The place where Saul stopped pursuing David because of the Philistine invasion
questions.explanation: Selahammahlekoth means 'The Rock of Division' or 'The Rock of Parting,' named because Saul turned back there to fight the Philistines instead of continuing to pursue David (1 Samuel 23:28).

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the contrasting pursuits of Saul and David on opposite sides of the mountain in 1 Samuel 23:26?
options: Chiasm illustrating tension and pursuit
Parallelism emphasizing their equal power
Foreshadowing David’s eventual victory
Inclusion framing David’s wilderness experience
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm illustrating tension and pursuit
questions.explanation: The narrative presents Saul and David on opposite sides of a mountain, a chiasm that highlights their tense pursuit and David’s desperate escape (1 Samuel 23:26). This literary structure enhances the drama of the chase.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ephod' refer to in the context of Abiathar bringing it to David?
options: A sacred garment used for inquiring of the LORD
A weapon for battle
A musical instrument for worship
A type of food provision
questions.correctAnswer: A sacred garment used for inquiring of the LORD
questions.explanation: The ephod was a priestly garment associated with the Urim and Thummim, used to seek God’s guidance, as Abiathar brought it to David to enquire of the LORD (1 Samuel 23:6, 9). This highlights the divine communication theme.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God delivering the faithful from their enemies as seen in 1 Samuel 23:14?
options: 2 Timothy 4:18
Matthew 5:10
John 3:16
Romans 8:28
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Timothy 4:18
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 4:18 speaks of the Lord delivering from every evil work, paralleling how God delivered David from Saul’s hand in 1 Samuel 23:14, showing divine protection of God's servants.

questions.question: How does the theme of covenant in 1 Samuel 23:18 connect with the broader biblical narrative?
options: It prefigures the Davidic Covenant and God's promises to David's descendants
It introduces the Mosaic Covenant for Israel’s law
It marks the first covenant with Abraham
It represents the New Covenant through Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the Davidic Covenant and God's promises to David's descendants
questions.explanation: The covenant between David and Jonathan foreshadows the Davidic Covenant (2 Samuel 7) where God promises an eternal kingdom through David’s lineage, fitting the theological development in Scripture.

questions.question: What was the significant cultural context behind the Ziphites' betrayal of David in 1 Samuel 23:19-20?
options: Local tribes often negotiated loyalties with reigning kings to maintain favor or avoid conflict
All tribes were united against Saul's enemies
The Ziphites were foreign invaders seeking to claim land
David had previously wronged the Ziphites in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Local tribes often negotiated loyalties with reigning kings to maintain favor or avoid conflict
questions.explanation: The Ziphites’ betrayal reflects the complex political loyalties in ancient Israel where local groups might side with the king to secure their own safety or favor, as seen in 1 Samuel 23:19-20.

questions.question: True or False: David remained in Keilah after defeating the Philistines and was never in danger of being betrayed by its inhabitants.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David had to leave Keilah because the LORD revealed that the men of Keilah would deliver him and his men into Saul’s hand, showing he was indeed in danger (1 Samuel 23:11-13).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan's encouragement to David that he would be king and Jonathan would be next to him was known by Saul.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David that Saul knew about his intentions and the future kingship, indicating Saul was aware of their covenant and David’s destined kingship (1 Samuel 23:17).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage foreshadows David's escape from Saul and his dwelling in strongholds, similar to 1 Samuel 23:29?
options: Psalm 57
Genesis 12
Exodus 20
Isaiah 53
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 57
questions.explanation: Psalm 57 is traditionally attributed to David during his flight from Saul, reflecting his refuge in caves and strongholds, paralleling the narrative in 1 Samuel 23:29 where David dwelt in strongholds at Engedi.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's assurance to David that the Philistines would be delivered into his hand at Keilah?
options: God's omniscience
God's sovereignty
God's mercy
God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 23:4 shows God's sovereign control over the outcome of battles by promising David that He will deliver the Philistines into his hand, demonstrating that God directs events according to His will.

questions.question: Which doctrine is reflected in David’s repeated inquiries of the LORD before taking action against the Philistines at Keilah?
options: Doctrine of divine providence
Doctrine of original sin
Doctrine of justification by faith
Doctrine of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine providence
questions.explanation: David enquiring of the LORD multiple times (1 Samuel 23:2, 23:4) shows his dependence on God's guidance, reflecting the doctrine that God providentially governs and directs His people’s actions.

questions.question: How does the covenant between David and Jonathan in this chapter contribute to the biblical theme of covenantal faithfulness?
options: It demonstrates human loyalty despite political rivalry
It shows the failure of God's promises
It highlights the need for legalistic adherence
It emphasizes isolation from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates human loyalty despite political rivalry
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 23:18 records the covenant between David and Jonathan, showing covenantal faithfulness and loyalty even amidst Saul’s opposition, reflecting the biblical theme of steadfast commitment despite adversity.

questions.question: What theological insight can be drawn from God not delivering David into Saul’s hand despite Saul’s continuous pursuit?
options: God’s protection of the anointed one
God’s indifference to human suffering
God’s impatience with disobedience
God’s condemnation of rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection of the anointed one
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 23:14 states God did not deliver David into Saul’s hand, demonstrating God’s protective care over His chosen servant, a foreshadowing of divine preservation of the Messiah’s lineage (Psalm 37:28).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do verses 10-12 convey about God’s omniscience and human responsibility?
options: God knows all events, yet humans must seek His guidance and act accordingly
God is unaware of human plans until revealed
Humans have full control over their destinies without divine knowledge
God’s foreknowledge removes human accountability
questions.correctAnswer: God knows all events, yet humans must seek His guidance and act accordingly
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 show David’s prayerful inquiry and God’s precise answers about Saul’s intentions and the men of Keilah, illustrating God’s omniscience alongside human responsibility to seek and obey divine direction.

questions.question: How does David's flight from Keilah after learning the townspeople would betray him illustrate biblical teaching on human sinfulness and divine deliverance?
options: It shows human treachery but God’s provision for escape
It reveals God’s abandonment of the faithful
It highlights that sin has no consequences
It demonstrates that trusting people is always safe
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human treachery but God’s provision for escape
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 23:12-13, David learns the men of Keilah will deliver him to Saul, revealing human sinfulness and betrayal; yet God enables David’s escape, underscoring divine deliverance despite human failings.

questions.question: What attribute of God is especially highlighted by the ephod's use in seeking divine guidance for David's safety?
options: God’s accessibility to prayer
God’s wrath
God’s immutability
God’s invisibility
questions.correctAnswer: God’s accessibility to prayer
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 23:9, David asks Abiathar to bring the ephod to inquire of the LORD, illustrating God's accessibility and willingness to communicate with His people through prayer and priestly mediation.

questions.question: In what way does Jonathan’s encouragement to David in the wilderness (verses 16-17) reflect a Christological typology?
options: Jonathan’s role as a faithful friend prefigures Christ’s intercessory support
Jonathan’s kingship replaces David’s
Jonathan’s betrayal foreshadows Judas
Jonathan’s silence predicts the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan’s role as a faithful friend prefigures Christ’s intercessory support
questions.explanation: Jonathan strengthening David’s hand and assuring his future kingship (1 Samuel 23:16-17) typologically foreshadows Christ’s intercessory role as the faithful friend and mediator who strengthens believers (Hebrews 7:25).

questions.question: How does Saul’s response to the Ziphites’ betrayal reveal the biblical tension between divine justice and human political ambition?
options: Saul’s gratitude to the Ziphites (v.21) shows political expediency overriding divine justice
Saul immediately repents for his sins
Saul seeks peace with David
Saul refuses to act on human reports
questions.correctAnswer: Saul’s gratitude to the Ziphites (v.21) shows political expediency overriding divine justice
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 23:21, Saul blesses the Ziphites for their 'compassion' in betraying David, revealing political motives often conflicting with God’s justice which ultimately protects the innocent anointed king.

questions.question: What synthesis of God’s providential protection and human obedience is revealed by the combined events of David’s escape from Saul and Saul’s redirected campaign against the Philistines?
options: God’s providence overrules human plans, and obedience includes trusting God’s timing
Human plans always triumph over God’s will
Obedience is unnecessary when God intervenes
God abandons His people in conflict
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence overrules human plans, and obedience includes trusting God’s timing
questions.explanation: Verses 26-28 show Saul pursuing David but being called away to fight the Philistines, and David escaping, illustrating God’s providential control over human affairs and the necessity of trusting His timing (1 Samuel 23:26-28).

questions.question: What does David’s reliance on the ephod and inquiry of the LORD teach about sanctification in the context of leadership under trial?
options: Sanctification involves dependence on God’s guidance amid adversity
Sanctification is achieved by human wisdom alone
Sanctification requires isolation from others
Sanctification means avoiding all conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves dependence on God’s guidance amid adversity
questions.explanation: David’s repeated inquiries to God using the ephod (1 Samuel 23:9) during Saul’s pursuit teach that sanctification in leadership includes ongoing dependence on God’s direction especially in trials.

questions.question: How does David’s experience in the wilderness strongholds reflect the biblical theme of God as refuge and fortress?
options: David’s dwelling in wilderness strongholds symbolizes God’s protection as a refuge for the faithful
David’s isolation indicates God’s rejection
David’s hiding shows human failure
David’s location is irrelevant to God’s protection
questions.correctAnswer: David’s dwelling in wilderness strongholds symbolizes God’s protection as a refuge for the faithful
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 23:14 and 23:29 show David abiding in wilderness strongholds, which typify God as a refuge and fortress for His people (Psalm 18:2), underscoring divine protection amid persecution.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 23:1-5 and 23:6, what does the narrative reveal about God's justice in relation to the oppressed inhabitants of Keilah?
options: God commands deliverance and salvation of the oppressed through David’s intervention
God allows the Philistines to oppress the innocent without consequence
God requires the inhabitants to fight alone
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God commands deliverance and salvation of the oppressed through David’s intervention
questions.explanation: Verses 1-5 describe God commanding David to save Keilah from the Philistines’ robbery, and verse 6 shows priestly support, revealing God’s justice in delivering the oppressed through His chosen leader.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s promise to deliver the Philistines into David’s hand (v.4) is mere human wishful thinking. What does 1 Samuel 23:4-5 actually teach about God’s providence and promise-keeping?
options: God sovereignly promises and accomplishes deliverance for His people
God’s promises are uncertain and subject to human change
Victory is solely due to human military strength
God remains silent in times of crisis
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly promises and accomplishes deliverance for His people
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 show God’s explicit promise to David to deliver the Philistines and David’s subsequent victory, teaching that God providentially governs events and faithfully keeps His promises (Psalm 33:10-11).

questions.question: What combined theological significance do verses 15 and 16 have regarding God’s providential care and the role of godly friendship?
options: God’s providential care is often mediated through faithful friendships that strengthen the believer
God’s providence excludes human relationships
Friendship is irrelevant to divine protection
God only protects those who isolate themselves
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential care is often mediated through faithful friendships that strengthen the believer
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 show David aware of Saul’s threat and Jonathan coming to strengthen him, revealing that God’s providence includes the ministry of godly friendships in sustaining His people (Ecclesiastes 4:9-10).
